title: Bessent Unveils 'Single Greatest Financial Offensive Ever' on Iran, Targets Banks and Trading Partners Aiding Tehran
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled what he called 'the single greatest financial offensive ever' against Iran, targeting countries, banks, and entities providing 'any type of lifeline' to Tehran — including oil-smuggling networks, currency swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, and front companies — with China's major banks singled out given Beijing's purchase of roughly 90% of Iran's oil exports historically. President Trump wrote 'IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!' and warned any country enabling Iran would face 'TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences.' Bessent told the Financial Times the goal was to 'sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime,' adding 'it is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime.' Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei warned 'any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences,' while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the move on social media as reminiscent of 2012-era sanctions: 'We have seen this movie before... Same bull. Different bullies.' Brent crude eased 1.3% to about $93/bbl on profit-taking as traders awaited the sanctions' full details.

title: Iran's Rial Hits Record Low as Sanctions Loom; Rice Up 60%, Beef Up 150% Since War Began
detail: Iran's rial currency hit a new record low as trading opened Monday, dropping to roughly 2.02 million to the US dollar on the open market — versus an official Central Bank rate near 1.5 million to the dollar — as Washington prepared to announce sweeping new sanctions. Currency trader Sadegh Mahmoudi, quoted at Tehran's Ferdowsi Square exchange hub, said 'there is no hope for a deal and peace.' President Trump wrote on social media that 'IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!' Nearly six months into the war, rice prices are up roughly 60% and beef prices up more than 150% since fighting began Feb 28, while the IMF forecasts an Iranian GDP contraction exceeding 5% for the year.
